clue.text: Prisoner, erstwhile one obeying the law?

blocks.note: a con is a convict, crossword shorthand for a prisoner
erstwhile means previous or onetime

explanation.surface: A jailbird who was once law-abiding, as if a career criminal had been a model citizen.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose and queried: anyone who conforms to a rule, a law included, could be called this.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who conforms follows the rules or accepted standards, so a law-abiding person fits as an example.

clue.text: Hit one displaying speed

blocks.note: first meaning: informal for strike or punch
second meaning: a dial such as a speedometer

explanation.walkthrough: A clock can be a dashboard dial such as a speedometer, as well as a timepiece.
explanation.definitionFit: To clock someone is British slang for punching them, and a car's speed dial is often called its clock.

clue.text: Poor tot languishes — these medical specialists may sort that out

indicators.note: sorting something out means rearranging it into a new order

blocks.note: all three words are the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A sick child is suffering, and doctors may be able to cure it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'sort that out' is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: These doctors study diseases of the nervous system, a branch of pathology.

clue.text: Where one may find dressing too tight

blocks.note: first meaning, read as two words: a bandage sits on top of an injury
second meaning: a spring or watch wound past its limit

explanation.surface: A bandage applied too tightly.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as OVER WOUND, the answer is where a dressing goes; as one word it is a clock or spring tightened excessively.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanism that has been overwound has had its spring coiled excessively tightly.

clue.text: Queen looked down upon by dull subject

indicators.note: in a down clue being looked down on means sitting below, so the queen comes after the dull word

blocks.note: matt describes a dull, non-glossy finish
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A monarch is scorned by a boring member of her people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject' suggests a royal subject; it means a topic.
explanation.definitionFit: The matter under discussion is the topic or theme being dealt with.

clue.text: 'Free NHS' — term abused in regeneration?

indicators.note: abused means misused or mangled, so the letters are mistreated into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A political slogan about free healthcare being misused in talk of renewal.
explanation.definitionFit: Refreshment is the restoring of energy or vigour, a renewal of strength.

clue.text: One month with a little fellow? Much longer than that!

blocks.note: Dec is the calendar abbreviation for December
taken as written
Des is a short form of the name Desmond, a small fellow's name

explanation.surface: Someone muses on spending a month with a small chap, then corrects the timescale to something far longer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays off the wordplay: a month is short, while the answer means stretches of ten years each.
explanation.definitionFit: Periods of ten years apiece are vastly longer spans of time than a single calendar month.

clue.text: Spooner's little woman no longer with us — having finished here?

indicators.note: Dr Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the first sounds of the two parts change places

blocks.clueFragment: little woman no longer with us
blocks.note: Beth is the March sister who dies in Little Women; say her name and dead with the opening sounds swapped

explanation.surface: A wife who has died, her life ended in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: BETH DEAD with the opening sounds swapped becomes DEATH BED; Beth famously dies in Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: A deathbed is where a person lies in their last hours, so where a life is finished.

clue.text: Torch in Home Counties implanted in top of hill

indicators.note: something implanted is set inside, so the counties abbreviation goes within the hilltop word

blocks.note: the crest is the summit of a hill
the Home Counties surround London in the South East of England

explanation.surface: A beacon lit on a hilltop in the countryside around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are those surrounding London, in England's south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: A cresset is an iron basket or cup holding burning fuel, used as a torch or beacon.

clue.text: Checkout in Norfolk town? Such will offer money off

indicators.note: the checkout sits inside the town's name

blocks.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk
a shop counter is where you pay

explanation.surface: A shop till in a small Norfolk town offering bargains.
explanation.walkthrough: Diss is a small market town in Norfolk, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Discounters are retailers selling goods cheaply, reducing prices below the usual level.

clue.text: PM laid up in short rest, being more tired than anyone else

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top, so the prime minister's name runs backwards
short means cut off, so the rest word loses its final letter
the reversed name sits inside the shortened rest word

blocks.note: Sir Robert Peel was a British prime minister
a siesta is an afternoon rest

explanation.surface: A prime minister bedridden during a brief nap, the most exhausted of all.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Robert Peel was a 19th-century British prime minister; in a down clue 'up' reads him bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepiest is the superlative of sleepy, so the drowsiest of all.

clue.text: Very energetic and touchy person fraying at the edges

indicators.note: when the phrase frays at both ends its outer letters wear away and only its middle stretch survives

blocks.note: the middle letters, with the outer ones of the two words worn off

explanation.surface: A highly strung, touchy individual seems to be coming apart at the seams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touchy person' reads as a description of the energetic one, but it is only the fodder: lose TOUC from the front and SON from the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyper is informal for overexcited or hyperactive, bursting with nervous energy.

clue.text: Explosive academic in charge, out for self-gratification

blocks.note: HE stands for high explosive
a don is a university teacher
IC is short for in charge

explanation.surface: A volatile professor in a position of power who is only interested in pleasing himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedonic relates to hedonism, the pursuit of pleasure, so is concerned with seeking enjoyment.

clue.text: Quiet church containing gold architectural feature

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the church abbreviation wraps the gold word

blocks.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
CH is the abbreviation for church
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A silent church with a gilded feature in its design.
explanation.definitionFit: A porch is a covered entrance structure built onto a house or church.

clue.text: Sorry poet, I worked in a dump?

indicators.note: worked means kneaded or reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An apologetic poet confesses to having had a job in a rubbish tip.
explanation.walkthrough: A dump is a place where things are deposited, which is what a repository is; hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A repository is a storage place where items are deposited, so a dump in a loose sense.

clue.text: Rich old university acquiring power fast

indicators.note: acquiring means taking something in, so the abbreviation for power is lodged inside the old university pair

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
P is the physics symbol for power
U is the usual abbreviation for university
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A wealthy old university gaining power quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like an adverb meaning quickly; here it is the noun, a period of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent describes lavish wealth and luxury, which is what being rich brings.

clue.text: Spread of food with litres for drinking

indicators.note: what is drunk goes inside the drinker, so the litres abbreviation is swallowed by the food word

blocks.note: fare is food, as in simple fare
L is the abbreviation for litres

explanation.surface: A spread of food laid out with litres of drink to wash it down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' suggests a buffet, which the surface reinforces; it means a widening, as in a flared skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A flare is a gradual widening outward, as of trouser legs or a skirt hem, so a spread.

clue.text: Regions across sea to the west, a hazard for travellers in haste?

definitions.text: a hazard for travellers in haste?

indicators.note: the regions stretch across the sea, lying on either side of it
in an across clue going west means moving right to left, so the assembled letters run backwards

blocks.note: parts of a country are its regions
the deep is a poetic name for the sea

explanation.surface: Lands straddling a western sea pose dangers for hasty travellers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The deep' is a poetic name for the sea. The whole assembly is read right to left at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Police set up these stretches with hidden cameras or radar to catch motorists who drive too fast.

clue.text: Understand what causes pain in Oxford maybe?

blocks.clueFragment: Understand what causes pain in Oxford maybe?
blocks.note: surface reading: grasp the source of suffering in the university city
setter's reading: an Oxford is a style of lace-up shoe, and the idiom is about knowing where a shoe hurts

explanation.surface: Someone diagnoses the root of distress in the city of Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford looks like the city; it is a type of shoe, which leads to the idiom for knowing the real source of a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means grasping exactly where a difficulty or hardship lies, from feeling a tight shoe press on the foot.

clue.text: Pretence by American to be a detective in his country

blocks.note: a sham is a pretence or fake
US is short for American, as in US citizen

explanation.surface: An American posing falsely as a detective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His country' points back to the American, telling the solver the word is US slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Shamus is old American slang for a private eye or police investigator.

clue.text: Doom's spelt out for this place

indicators.note: spelt out suggests the letters are laid out afresh, in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Destruction is announced for a doomed place.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a description: in Genesis God destroys Sodom by fire and brimstone.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodom is the biblical city of the plain destroyed for its wickedness, the place that was doomed.

clue.text: Number going round at noon are menacing

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so the number wraps around the word at

blocks.note: a number spelt out
taken as written
N is short for noon

explanation.surface: A group circling at midday looks menacing, like a showdown in a western.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is plural, matching the verb 'are', so the answer is read as 'they threaten'.
explanation.definitionFit: To threaten is to pose a menace or danger, so a plural subject that threatens is menacing.

clue.text: Fellows getting rid of leader sing to show delight

indicators.note: the leader is the front letter, and getting rid of it drops the first letter of the fellows word

blocks.note: fellows are men
to chant is to sing in a repeated, rhythmic way

explanation.surface: A group of men, minus their leader, burst into song to express joy.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant someone is to charm or captivate them, filling them with pleasure, so to delight them.

clue.text: High-up boss may be here, but it's a precarious location for a cradle

annotation.answer: AT THE TOP OF THE TREE

definitions.text: a precarious location for a cradle

blocks.note: first meaning: the highest position in an organisation

blocks.clueFragment: a precarious location for a cradle
blocks.note: second meaning: where the nursery rhyme Rock-a-bye Baby puts the cradle

explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme begins 'Rock-a-bye baby, on the tree top', and the cradle falls when the bough breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for the most senior level of a profession, and literally the highest branches.

clue.text: Something smoked became item of food

blocks.note: fag is British slang for a cigarette
got, as in got angry, means became

explanation.surface: Smoked meat turning into food.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a faggot is a meatball of minced offal, and a fag is a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A faggot is a traditional British savoury meatball made from pork offal and bread.

clue.text: At sea they'd dread being like the Ancient Mariner?

indicators.note: at sea means confused and lost, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Sailors far from land fear ending up like Coleridge's cursed seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: In Coleridge's poem the Mariner is becalmed with 'water, water, everywhere, nor any drop to drink'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mariner and his crew suffered terrible thirst with no fresh water, so they were parched and lacking fluid.

clue.text: Wearing garment with one gun, soldiers who may be on the prowl?

definitions.text: who may be on the prowl?

blocks.note: dressed in something means wearing it
a vest is an undergarment
I is the Roman numeral for one
gat is old American slang for a pistol
OR stands for other ranks, the ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Armed soldiers in vests, one carrying a gun, sound like a patrol on the lookout.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a loose, queried description: detectives prowl around seeking clues.
explanation.definitionFit: Detectives and other inquiry agents may roam and nose about looking for evidence, rather like a prowler.

clue.text: French port's name engraved in seat

indicators.note: an engraving is cut into a surface, so the name letter is set within the seat word

explanation.walkthrough: Seat looks like furniture but means the backside, here its Latin anatomical name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nantes is a city on the Loire in western France, historically a major port.

clue.text: Court of King Arthur

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters taken from within the following words

blocks.note: letters sitting across the two words

explanation.surface: Camelot, the court of the legendary king.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to Camelot; the answer sits in plain sight across the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A garth is an enclosed yard or courtyard, especially one in a cloister.

clue.text: Repeated shout of disapproval for mistake

indicators.note: repeated means said twice, so the jeering word is written down two times

blocks.note: a jeer from the crowd
the same jeer again

explanation.surface: A crowd jeers again and again at someone's blunder.

clue.text: Greek island produces items of fruit, any number going to waste

clue.text: Opening of a test's beginning at the southern end

blocks.note: taken as written
the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for cars

explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's yearly safety test for vehicles. Read from the bottom, A MOTS becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoma is a mouth-like pore in a leaf or an artificial opening made in surgery.

clue.text: Swallow to obtain feathers

blocks.note: first meaning: manage to swallow food or drink
second meaning: acquire the soft feathers called down

explanation.surface: A swallow gathering feathers, perhaps to line its nest.
explanation.walkthrough: Swallow looks like the bird, which fits the feathers; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To get food down is to swallow it, and getting the fine under-plumage of a bird is literally acquiring down.

clue.text: Sarah joins the stars — they get paid

blocks.note: Sal is a pet form of Sarah
Aries is a constellation and star sign

explanation.surface: A woman named Sarah becomes a celebrity, and celebrities are well paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joins the stars' suggests fame; it is just the constellation. The definition stretches: these are the sums that get paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Salaries are fixed regular wages handed over to employees, so they are what gets paid.

clue.text: Poet messin' about

blocks.note: first meaning: Philip ..., English poet
second meaning: larking about, with the dropped g

clue.text: A good number remain endlessly uncertain about what to believe

G is the abbreviation for good
No. is the abbreviation for number

explanation.walkthrough: 'A good number' reads as 'many', but it splits into A, G and NO.

clue.text: Firm with fashion festival — one has flowers

the Christian spring festival

explanation.walkthrough: S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded. Geoffrey de Havilland founded the aircraft firm that built the Mosquito.

clue.text: Headgear for criminals in US districts

clue.text: Weapon to throw or shoot

clue.text: Vessel to meander with someone blocking radio messages

clue.text: Kitchenware chipped on top used for garden feature
